headline: SSC & equivalent exam results for 2026 to be published today, August 10
summary: Students can access their results starting 10 AM via SMS and through the official websites of all education boards.
details: The results of the 2026 SSC and equivalent examinations are set to be released today, Monday, August 10. The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee made this announcement on Saturday, August 8.
Students will be able to access their results starting from 10 AM. They can check their scores through SMS services or by visiting the official websites of their respective education boards.
caption:
The wait is over! SSC and equivalent exam results for 2026 are out today, August 10, at 10 AM.

The results of the 2026 SSC and equivalent examinations are set to be released today, Monday, August 10. The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee made this announcement on Saturday, August 8.

Students will be able to access their results starting from 10 AM. They can check their scores through SMS services or by visiting the official websites of their respective education boards.

headline_marked: [[16 Bangladeshis killed]] in devastating Saudi sofa factory fire in Riyadh
headline: 16 Bangladeshis killed in devastating Saudi sofa factory fire in Riyadh
summary: A massive fire engulfed a sofa factory in Riyadh's Musa Industrial Area, claiming the lives of at least 16 Bangladeshi nationals. Rescue operations were ongoing as authorities worked to identify the victims.
details: At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh. The incident occurred around 2:00 PM yesterday in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station.
The Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry confirmed the deaths, quoting fire service personnel. Witnesses stated that all victims were from Bangladesh.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh expressed deep sorrow and confirmed officials are on site. They are in close contact with Saudi authorities to identify the victims.

Earlier reports from Expatriates’ Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury indicated seven workers from Naogaon’s Atrai upazila were among the deceased. Other reports mentioned 10 from Naogaon and 3 from Natore.
caption:
At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals have tragically died in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The Expatriates' Welfare Ministry confirmed the fatalities.

At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh. The incident occurred around 2:00 PM yesterday in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station.

The Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry confirmed the deaths, quoting fire service personnel. Witnesses stated that all victims were from Bangladesh.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh expressed deep sorrow and confirmed officials are on site. They are in close contact with Saudi authorities to identify the victims.

Earlier reports from Expatriates’ Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury indicated seven workers from Naogaon’s Atrai upazila were among the deceased. Other reports mentioned 10 from Naogaon and 3 from Natore.

Source: Jamuna TV, The Daily Star
